title: Hyperloop SDK Onramp — Playbook + Experiment Manifest
body:
Purpose:
A compact, reproducible onramp for new internal integrators and pilots that gets a sandboxed SDK environment, a verified prompt canon, and a smoke-telemetry baseline in under 15 minutes.

High-level goals:
- Hands-on quickstart with minimal friction: spin up local sdkenv, run 3 smoke flows (hello world generate, chat session, embeddings lookup).
- Provide a small curated prompt canon for onboarding that demonstrates safety, hallucination checks, and structured outputs.
- Fail-fast diagnostics and telemetry hooks so first 50 requests produce usable traces/cost breakdown.

Non-goals:
- Full production hardening (this is a pilot/onramp, not an ops runbook).
- Exhaustive model tuning guidance.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Time-to-first-successful-token from signup < 15 minutes (measured in lab run).
- 80% of pilot teams can run at least 1 of the 3 smoke flows without engineer assistance.
- Telemetry captured for request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, token_count, failure_reason for first 100 requests.

Minute-0 checklist (operator):
1) Provision sandbox API key (dev tier).
2) Clone sdkenv starter: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/hyperloop-onramp
3) Run ./scripts/quick-provision.sh (local docker compose + mock creds).
4) Start smoke harness: python tools/smoke_harness.py --flow hello|chat|embed
5) Open Console > Playgrounds > "Hyperloop Pilot" to watch traces.
Notes-to-self: quick-provision should be <60s on m1/m2 dev laptop; if not, break into 2 steps.

Verified prompt canon (short):
- Smoke: "Summarize the following text in 2 bullets." (used for canonical token baseline)
- Safety-check: "Identify any hallucinated facts and mark them as HYPOTHESIS."
- Structured output: "Return JSON with keys [title, summary, sources] only."
Each prompt has a t-shirt size (S/M/L) for expected token usage. See appendix links in Confluence.

Three starter flows (what we demo):
A) Hello generate (sync):
- Purpose: validate auth/latency/cost measurement.
- SDK snippet: r = client.generate(prompt="Summarize...", max_tokens=80)
- Expected telemetry: latency < 400ms on dev tier, tokens_out < 120

B) Conversational demo (streaming):
- Purpose: validate streaming hooks and partial rendering in UI.
- Flow: client.chat.stream(messages=[...]) -> UI shows partial chunks -> final chunk triggers structured parse.
- Failure mode: stream drop -> fallback to non-streaming generation and emit alert tag stream_fallback.

C) Embeddings + local retrieval (mini RAG):
- Purpose: demonstrate embeddings generation and similarity lookup using SQLite example index.
- Steps: generate embeddings -> upsert to local index -> query -> rank by cosine -> generate answer with source citations.

Failure modes & recovery heuristics (quick):
- 401/invalid key: throw clear error and open quick-provision steps.
- 429 burst: apply client-side linear backoff and mark telemetry span as throttled.
- Model mismatch: if tokens exceed expected t-shirt size, automatically downgrade to a cheaper variant and tag quality_regression.

Telemetry gating (required fields):
- request_id, user_email (redacted), model_variant, sequence_length_in, sequence_length_out, latency_ms, cost_usd_est, status, failure_reason, sandbox_id
- Attach minimal prompt hash (SHA1) for prompt-regression grouping.

Experiment manifest (3 quick experiments to run during pilot):
1) Prompt brevity A/B: canonical summarizer vs. explicit constraints (2 bullets + max 40 tokens). Metric: tokens_out and user_estimated_quality (1–5). Owner: Benji.
2) Stream vs Poll UX: compare perceived latency (survey) and actual time-to-first-byte. Owner: Evelyn.
3) Cache policy test: enable prefix-KV cache for repeated queries and measure 1k-run cost delta. Owner: Marco.
Each experiment has a 3-day runtime target and a simple dashboard template in the Console.

Rollout plan (mini):
- Day 0: internal dev run (authors only).
- Day 3: 5 pilot teams (invite-only).
- Day 10: open self-serve for org-wide devs (feature flag: hyperloop_onramp_enabled).
- Rollback: if rollout shows >10% error increase or cost exceed budget threshold, flip flag off and notify owners.

Open questions / risky assumptions:
- Does dev tier mirror production quant/latency enough to be meaningful? (Action: prod infra to provide sample cost profile).
- How to safely store prompt canon without leaking customer input into corpus? (Action: data governance to advise).

Appendix: quick debug commands
- tail -f /var/log/sdkenv/proxy.log | grep sandbox_id
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"Summarize x"}'
- python tools/collect_trace.py --request-id <id> > /tmp/trace.json

Next steps (owners):
- Benji: finalize quick-provision script + test matrix (due 2024-11-12).
- Marco: embed sqlite retrieval example and bench harness (due 2024-11-15).
- Evelyn: telemetry dashboard templates + survey page (due 2024-11-18).

Quick links / references:
- Confluence: Hyperloop Onramp Index (linked above)
- Slack: #devx-hyperloop (thread: convo/UX-feedback-11-03)
- GH: PR list /compare/hyperloop-onramp

Unpolished notes:
- Might include a tiny web UI that shows streaming tokens live + cost counter.
- Consider shipping a "first-run" disposable sandbox that tears down automatically after 24h to reduce cost risk.

-- end of playbook manifest (working draft)
